stories.head: Trump, Xi and Putin pledge to cut nuclear risks after rare three-way talks
stories.say: Donald Trump, Xi Jinping and Vladimir Putin met for about ninety minutes in Shenzhen on Thursday, agreeing that a nuclear war cannot be won and pledging to boost oil and gas supply.
stories.stand: The leaders of the US, China and Russia met for about 90 minutes in Shenzhen, but their joint statement left out Ukraine and the Korean Peninsula.
body: Donald Trump, Xi Jinping and Vladimir Putin met for about 90 minutes in Shenzhen on Thursday, on the sidelines of the APEC summit. It was the first such three-way meeting.

A joint statement released by the Kremlin, and later by the White House, said the leaders reaffirmed that there can be no winners in a nuclear war. They also committed to raising oil and gas supply, with no targets or timelines given.

Chinese state broadcaster CCTV's readout said state officials' immunity should be respected and that the International Criminal Court should not abuse its jurisdiction. Putin faces an ICC arrest warrant over the alleged deportation of Ukrainian children.
Putin ruled out direct talks with Ukraine, citing a Ukrainian strike on the Kerch Bridge earlier in the week. Trump called Putin his 'friend' and left China without meeting North Korea's Kim Jong-un.

stories.head: Trump questions European spending on Ukraine in call to allies, Politico reports
stories.say: Hours after meeting Vladimir Putin, Donald Trump reportedly phoned Ukraine's European allies and asked why they were still spending billions on military aid, according to Politico.
stories.stand: European officials told Politico that Trump called a meeting of Ukraine's allies and said Putin was serious about peace talks.
body: Donald Trump unexpectedly phoned a meeting of Ukraine's European allies on Thursday and asked why they were still spending billions on military support for Kyiv, according to Politico, which cited four briefed European officials.
The call came hours after Trump met Vladimir Putin and Xi Jinping in Shenzhen. Officials said Trump insisted Putin was serious about future peace talks.
Three officials said Trump was strongly sceptical of further aid from the Coalition of the Willing, a group of 34 countries plus Ukraine. There was no on-record comment from the White House.

stories.head: UN top court rules Myanmar committed genocide against the Rohingya
stories.say: The International Court of Justice has ruled, by nine votes to six, that Myanmar committed genocide against the Rohingya, the first time it has found a state responsible.
stories.stand: The International Court of Justice ruled 9-6 in a case brought by The Gambia in 2019, the first time it has found a state committed genocide.
body: The International Court of Justice in The Hague ruled on Thursday, by 9 votes to 6, that Myanmar committed genocide against the Rohingya in northern Rakhine state.

Court president Yuji Iwasawa said Myanmar's security forces killed thousands of Rohingya civilians. Both outlets report the court cited evidence of about 10,000 deaths. The court rejected Myanmar's argument that its 2017 campaign was lawful action against insurgents.
The Gambia brought the case in 2019. The court ordered reparations, including help for safe returns. About 1.2 million Rohingya refugees live in Bangladesh, mostly in camps at Cox's Bazar.
The ruling is final and binding, but the court can only report non-compliance to the UN Security Council.

stories.head: Houthi attack damages tower in Riyadh's financial district
stories.say: Saudi civil defence says a Houthi attack damaged several floors of a tower in Riyadh's financial district on Thursday. No one was hurt, and air defences later destroyed four more missiles.
stories.stand: Saudi authorities said no one was injured; the Saudi-led coalition later said it destroyed four ballistic missiles fired at the south.
body: A Houthi attack damaged a tower in Riyadh's financial district on Thursday, Saudi Arabia's civil defence said. It reported damage to several floors and nearby buildings but no injuries.
The statement did not name the building. A photo released by authorities appears to show the Public Investment Fund tower, The New Arab reported.

Hours later, coalition spokesman Maj Gen Turki al-Maliki said air defences destroyed four ballistic missiles fired at the southern border region. The Houthis claimed strikes on Riyadh's airport and financial centre.
The World Health Organization says the escalation in Yemen since August has killed 2,260 people. UNICEF says more than 330,000 people have been displaced.

stories.head: Trump says Iran may be looking at biological or chemical weapons
stories.say: Donald Trump says there are signs Iran is looking at biological or chemical weapons, though officials disagree on the intelligence. He says he's not rushing a decision.
stories.stand: Officials disagree over the intelligence, and Trump told Israeli TV he was 'not rushing' a decision on Iran.
body: Donald Trump told Fox News there is 'indication' that Iran is looking at biological or chemical weapons. The New York Times reports US and Israeli officials cite intelligence on this, but disagree over how strong it is.
Trump told Israel's Channel 12 he was 'not rushing to make any decisions on Iran'. He also said he would 'see what happens' after 1 January.

The Pentagon's deputy comptroller said the war has cost more than $48 billion since February. The UK Maritime Trade Operations centre confirmed a tanker was hit by an unknown projectile near Khasab, Oman, on Wednesday.

stories.head: Danish parliament approves Greenland security deal with the US
stories.say: Denmark's parliament has voted 109 to nil to approve a security deal with the United States covering Greenland. It lets the US expand its military presence on the island.
stories.stand: The vote was 109-0, and the deal lets the US set up new defence areas while Greenland stays under Danish control.
body: Denmark's parliament voted 109-0 on Thursday to approve a security agreement with the United States covering Greenland. Greenland's parliament approved it earlier in November.
The deal, signed in New York in September, builds on a 1951 defence agreement. It lets the US expand activities at Pituffik Space Base and set up defence areas at Narsarsuaq and Mestersvig.
Al Jazeera reports it also bars countries outside the EU and NATO from strategic sectors. It is not a treaty, so it needs no US Senate vote, and takes effect once Denmark notifies Washington.
Greenland stays under Danish control, and the deal would still apply if Greenland became independent.

stories.head: North Korea is expanding a uranium enrichment site, IAEA chief says
stories.say: The head of the UN nuclear watchdog, Rafael Grossi, says North Korea is extending its original enrichment facility at Yongbyon, calling it a cause for serious concern.
stories.stand: Rafael Grossi said the extension at Yongbyon was externally complete by late October, based on satellite imagery.
body: North Korea is extending its original uranium enrichment facility at Yongbyon, International Atomic Energy Agency head Rafael Grossi told the agency's board of governors.
Grossi said construction began in mid-September and the extension was externally complete by late October. He called it 'a cause for serious concern'.
The IAEA has had no access to North Korean sites since inspectors were expelled in 2009. It relies on satellite imagery and open-source information.
Secretary of State Marco Rubio said no meeting between Donald Trump and Kim Jong-un was scheduled.

stories.head: Dozens missing after migrant boat sinks off Senegal
stories.say: A boat carrying around a hundred migrants bound for Spain capsized off Senegal early on Wednesday. At least one person died and dozens are missing, local officials say.
stories.stand: The boat was carrying around 100 people towards Spain's Canary Islands when it capsized off the town of Yenne.
body: A boat carrying around 100 migrants capsized off Senegal in the early hours of Wednesday while trying to reach Spain, local officials said. At least one person died and dozens are missing.
An official at the mayor's office in Yenne, south of Dakar, said the accident happened around 3am. Firefighters recovered one body and police arrested one survivor.
Spanish government figures show more than 11,000 migrants reached the Canary Islands in the first half of November. Senegal's navy said it had rescued over 1,400 migrants at sea in 48 hours.

stories.say: Iraq's prime minister has given the Iran-backed group Kataib Hezbollah until Friday to leave Jurf al-Nasr, south of Baghdad, after a committee looked into alleged oil smuggling.
stories.stand: The government says the move targets oil smuggling; the group rejects the allegation and says it will not leave.
body: Iraq's Prime Minister Ali Faleh al-Zaidi has given Iran-backed Kataib Hezbollah until Friday to leave Jurf al-Nasr, in Babil province about 100km south of Baghdad.
A source told the Iraqi News Agency that army, police and other units will redeploy there when the deadline expires. A government spokesman said the plan targets anyone exploiting Iraq's oil wealth.
Kataib Hezbollah rejects the smuggling allegations. A senior figure said the group would not leave, while saying it did not want bloodshed.

stories.head: Ecuadorian fishermen sue US government over alleged drone strike
stories.say: Sixteen Ecuadorian fishermen are suing the US for at least five million dollars, saying drones from a US-operated ship sank their boat in March.
stories.stand: The 16 men say drones from a US-operated ship sank their boat in March; the US military has not claimed responsibility.
body: Sixteen Ecuadorian fishermen have sued the US government in a court in Pennsylvania, seeking at least $5 million in damages, Reuters reports.
The men say two drones launched from a US-operated ship struck their boat on 17 March, setting crew members alight and sinking it. They also allege mistreatment afterwards.
The US military has not claimed responsibility. Ecuador's navy inspected the boat and cleared it of wrongdoing, and the men deny any cartel links.

stories.head: Five EU countries agree in principle to open a deportation hub in Rwanda
stories.say: Germany, Denmark, Austria, Greece and the Netherlands have agreed in principle with Rwanda to open a return hub there in 2027, for migrants who've exhausted their right to stay.
stories.stand: Germany, Denmark, Austria, Greece and the Netherlands want to open the 'return hub' in 2027 for people with deportation orders.
body: Germany, Denmark, Austria, Greece and the Netherlands have reached an agreement in principle with Rwanda to open a 'return hub' there in 2027.
It would apply only to migrants who have exhausted legal options to stay and have a deportation order. Those sent could stay in Rwanda or return home.
Danish Prime Minister Mette Frederiksen called it 'a crucial step'. The Danish Refugee Council said it was 'deeply concerned', and Amnesty International criticised the plan.

stories.head: Kenya's milk shortage deepens as drought hits dairy farmers
stories.say: Kenya's milk shortage is getting worse as dry weather hits dairy farmers. One farmer says her daily output has fallen from a hundred and twenty litres to fifty.
stories.stand: Farmers report sharp falls in output, and Agriculture Secretary Mutahi Kagwe blames prolonged dry conditions.
body: A drought is deepening Kenya's milk shortage, with farmers reporting sharp falls in output and some Nairobi shops raising prices, Al Jazeera reports.
One farmer in Kajiado County said her daily output fell from 120 litres to 50. A cooperatives official said at least five women-led dairy groups reported a 50% drop in deliveries.
Agriculture Cabinet Secretary Mutahi Kagwe blamed prolonged dry conditions. The government says it is expanding fodder and providing milk coolers to farmer groups.

stories.head: Florida pastor convicted over plot to kill Haiti's president
stories.say: A Florida pastor, Christian Emmanuel Sanon, has been found guilty in Miami over the plot that led to the killing of Haiti's president Jovenel Moïse in 2021. His lawyer says he'll appeal.
stories.stand: A Miami jury found Christian Emmanuel Sanon guilty on all eight charges; his lawyer says he will appeal.
body: A federal jury in Miami found Florida pastor Christian Emmanuel Sanon guilty on all eight charges over the plot that led to the killing of Haiti's President Jovenel Moïse.
The most serious charge is conspiracy to kidnap or kill a person outside the US. He faces up to life in prison. Prosecutors said he was the conspirators' first choice to replace Moïse.
Sanon denied knowing of plans to kill the president. His lawyer said he would appeal. Moïse was killed in a raid on his home on 7 July 2021.

US Southern Command says more than 300 US soldiers recently trained with 400 Colombian troops.

stories.head: Four men guilty of sexual offences against woman drugged by her husband
stories.say: Four men have been found guilty at Winchester Crown Court of sexual offences, including rape, against a woman whose then-husband drugged her and recruited strangers online.
stories.stand: The woman's former husband, Philip Young, had already admitted dozens of offences including 11 counts of rape.
body: Four men were found guilty at Winchester Crown Court on Thursday of sexual offences, including rape, against a woman at her home in Swindon. They had been recruited online.

Her then-husband, Philip Young, a former councillor, had pleaded guilty to dozens of offences, including 11 counts of rape and 11 counts of administering a substance with intent. Another defendant had also admitted offences.
The judge, Mr Justice Pushpinder Saini, said the men face significant prison sentences. The men had argued they believed she consented.
The woman, who has waived her right to anonymity, urged other victims to come forward.

body: Google has rejected a Ministry of Justice request to remove a YouTube video in which Russell Brand says he is innocent, the BBC reported. Google reportedly found its rules had not been broken.

Brand is serving a sentence of ten and a half years for rape and other offences. His wife read his message on their YouTube podcast on Sunday, prompting an investigation into whether he broke prison rules.
Housing minister Matthew Pennycook said the government does not have the power to mandate removal. The Ministry of Justice said YouTube should take the content down.

body: The High Court has granted Birmingham City Council an interim injunction banning unauthorised flags on lampposts, bridges and roundabouts across the city.

Judge Emma Kelly said the court was not banning the Union Jack or pride flags. Breaching the order could lead to up to two years in prison or a fine.

stories.say: Billy Allison has been found guilty at Stafford Crown Court of murdering Matthew O'Gara with a punch to the neck in a Lichfield bar in May. He'll be sentenced on the fifth of January.
stories.stand: Billy Allison punched Matthew O'Gara from behind in a Lichfield bar in May; jurors were not told he belonged to Raise the Colours.
body: Billy Allison, 36, has been found guilty at Stafford Crown Court of murdering Matthew O'Gara, 44, at a bar in Lichfield on 24 May.

The court heard Allison punched Mr O'Gara in the side of the neck from behind, breaking bones and splitting an artery. He died two days later in hospital. Allison was also convicted of grievous bodily harm against a second man.
Allison told the court it was 'a moment of madness'. Jurors were not told he was a member of the Raise the Colours group. He will be sentenced on 5 January.

stories.stand: The local MP says the Home Office told him the Mercure Hotel near Dumfries will close in February 2027.
body: The Mercure Hotel near Dumfries, which has housed asylum seekers since 2023, will close in February 2027, according to Dumfries and Galloway MP John Cooper.
He shared a Home Office letter linking the closure to the government's plan to end the use of asylum hotels. Residents are to be moved beforehand, ideally to dispersed accommodation.
Home Secretary Shabana Mahmood has said the government aims to end hotel use for asylum seekers by the end of this Parliament.

stories.say: Jersey's government says it is owed forty point two million pounds after some employers took tax and social security from workers' pay but never passed it on.
stories.stand: Jersey's government says it is owed £40.2 million in unpaid deductions, and tribunal cases on the issue have risen more than 500%.

stories.head: Tall Antarctic ice cliffs retreat fast but then stabilise, study finds
stories.say: Satellite data on more than fifteen thousand Antarctic ice cliffs shows tall cliffs can retreat faster than models predicted, but the retreat was short-lived and the glaciers stabilised.
stories.stand: MIT and Woods Hole researchers tracked more than 15,000 cliffs with NASA's ICESat-2 satellite.
body: Researchers at MIT and Woods Hole Oceanographic Institution tracked more than 15,000 Antarctic ice cliffs using NASA's ICESat-2 satellite from 2019 to 2023, a study in Science reports.
At four sites with cliffs around 100 metres tall, glaciers retreated faster than models predicted. But the retreat was short-lived and the glaciers stabilised.
Sea ice, iceberg debris and underwater ridges appear to help stabilise the cliffs. The researchers say this matters for sea-level projections.

stories.head: Lyon housing block designed to need no heating or air conditioning
stories.say: A seven-storey housing block in Lyon has been designed to stay between twenty and twenty-eight degrees without heating or air conditioning, using walls sixty-one centimetres thick.
stories.stand: The 23-flat building in Lyon has 61cm walls; the developer says bills fall 80%, but a councillor says it cannot be scaled up.

It aims to keep indoor temperatures at 20-22°C in winter and 26-28°C in heatwaves, using walls and floors 61cm thick.
Developer Nexity says energy bills fall by 80%. A Lyon councillor, Renaud Payre, said the project cannot be replicated on a large scale.

stories.head: Rare stonefly found beside vanishing glacier near Cape Horn
stories.say: Scientists have found a rare stonefly beside the remains of a glacier on Chile's Navarino Island, near Cape Horn. It matches no known species and may be new to science.
stories.stand: The insect from Navarino Island matches no known species, researchers report in the journal Ecology.
body: Scientists have found a rare stonefly beside the remnants of a glacier on Navarino Island, in Chile's Tierra del Fuego archipelago near Cape Horn.
The insect matches no known species and may be undescribed, according to a study in the journal Ecology led by Javier Rendoll-Cárcamo.
Researchers from the University of Magallanes, the University of Barcelona and the British Antarctic Survey took part. Whether it lives only in this area is not yet known.

stories.stand: The FAA and L3Harris concluded a site in El Dorado, Arkansas, where a new router was being installed, caused the outage.
body: Contractor L3Harris took several hours to pinpoint the source of the outage that caused last Friday's nationwide US ground stop, a person familiar with the investigation told CBS News.

Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy said the failure to quickly identify and isolate the problem concerned him.

body: Vincent van Gogh's 'Chestnut Trees in Bloom', painted in 1890, sold at Sotheby's in New York for a record for the artist, Euronews reports. An image caption gives the price as $190.4 million.

The AIU also banned Veronica Loleo for three years and Ronald Korir for six years.

stories.say: Rassie Erasmus, banned for six matches for questioning officials, will host an online watch-along of South Africa's game against Ireland on Saturday.

body: Springboks coach Rassie Erasmus, banned for six matches by World Rugby for questioning officials, will host an online watch-along of Saturday's match against Ireland in Dublin.

stories.head: Malaysian weightlifting champion loses arm after motorbike crash
stories.say: Malaysia's Commonwealth Games weightlifting champion Muhammad Hafizuddin Roslin has had his right arm amputated after a motorbike crash. His federation says he's stable, awake and smiling.
stories.stand: The 21-year-old Commonwealth Games gold medallist is in a stable condition after seven hours of surgery.
body: Malaysian weightlifter Muhammad Hafizuddin Roslin, a Commonwealth Games gold medallist, has had his right arm amputated above the elbow after a motorbike crash, according to local media.
The 21-year-old crashed on an expressway on Monday night. After seven hours of surgery in Kuala Lumpur he is stable, and his federation's president said he was 'awake and smiling'.
He won gold in the 88kg category at the Glasgow Commonwealth Games. The government will cover his treatment costs.

stories.head: Ecuadorian footballer banned for eight years for hitting referee with rock
stories.say: Ecuador's football federation has banned Jhon Perlaza for eight years after he threw a stone that hit an assistant referee during a third-tier match in October.
stories.stand: The federation says the official needed surgery; it will ask FIFA to extend the ban worldwide.
body: Ecuador's football federation has banned Jhon Perlaza from all football activity for eight years, until October 2034, Reuters reports.
During a third-tier match on 17 October, he threw a stone that struck an assistant referee. The federation said the official needed surgery and 60 days to recover.
The federation will ask FIFA to extend the ban worldwide. His club apologised and said it removed him.

stories.head: India complains over alleged racist gesture in under-17 match against Palestine
stories.say: India's football federation has asked the Asian Football Confederation to review an alleged racist gesture by a Palestinian player during an under-17 qualifier. The player denies it.
stories.stand: The Palestinian player says the gesture was a reaction to the humidity; India won the qualifier 4-1.
body: The All India Football Federation has asked the Asian Football Confederation to review footage of an alleged racist gesture by a Palestinian player in an under-17 qualifier in Kuala Lumpur.
India won the match 4-1. The player denied the accusation, saying the gesture was a reaction to the humidity.
The AFC has not publicly acknowledged the complaint.
